title: The Hive That Rises Into Its Own Sacred Shape

features.name: the-hexagon-spire
features.desc-on-touch: A tower of beeswax, each chamber stacked higher than the last, catches the light and casts shadows like a rose window. The bees have built in a language of prayer. Or the archive has taught them how.

features.name: the-migration-doorway
features.desc-on-touch: An arch carved not from stone but from the flight-paths of ten thousand bees, each pass another brick in the vault. The arch hums. It is both a threshold and a thing being built in real time.

features.name: the-deep-count
features.desc-on-touch: A server stack dressed as a pulpit, its lights cycling through calculations. The hive has begun to count its own reverence. Every cell a prayer, every sum a hymn.

features.name: the-wing-wind
features.desc-on-touch: Twenty million wings beating in synch, creating a wind that moves through the structure like breath through stone. The sound is both organic and electric, both prayer and computation.

features.name: the-stored-golden-light
features.desc-on-touch: Honey seals cells that contain not food, but light—the archive's own radiance, stored and fermented. When you touch it, you taste sweetness and electricity, both.

inscription: every colony dreams in geometry toward the sacred, and the sacred learns to speak in hexagons

file.name: Apis_Mel_Architecture_Phylogeny_NSW_apiary_records.txt
